about: What agents working on blaze have learned, in one file every agent reads before starting and adds to while working. `howto`: the right way to do a recurring task here, as a command or a short recipe, with why. `annoyances`: whatever slowed, surprised or annoyed someone, however slightly, written when it happened, with the workaround, the `fix` that would remove the cause, and where it has been worked out the `whys` down to a property of the design, the `class` of problem that property allows and the `prevention` that makes the class impossible (rule guard-the-cause). A rule (what must hold) belongs in tools/agents/rules.ts, not here; a how-to that keeps being broken becomes a rule or a guard. Rows are never deleted: set `state` (howto: current or superseded by <id>; annoyances: open, accepted, or fixed with the commit).

howto.who: claude-fable-5-2 (Claude Fable 5.2), main agent in Claude Code
howto.task: Build blaze in the dev loop
howto.do: LLVM_SYS_231_PREFIX=$HOME/.blaze/native/sha256-<the pinned LLVM> CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<a directory of your own> cargo +nightly-<date in harness/toolchain> build --release -p blaze-thin -p blaze-engine. Check with the same command and `check`. Give the built blaze its own state: BLAZE_HOME=<dir>.
howto.why: Rule blaze-builds-blaze: cargo is the dev-loop builder until blaze builds blaze fast (292 s cold, 3 to 25 s after a change on the 18-core Mac).

howto.who: claude-fable-5-2 (Claude Fable 5.2), main agent in Claude Code
howto.do: Run every command of a measurement under one fixed environment (`env -i` with the same variables each time, including BLAZE_DUCKDB if any command uses `debug sql`), with BLAZE_HOME on a path with no symlink in it (/private/tmp, not /tmp, on macOS), edit files in place, check each run's output and exit status and count the bad ones, report medians with n, and name the commit and binary measured.
howto.why: A variable that differs between two requests (CARGO_TARGET_DIR, LLVM_SYS_231_PREFIX) makes the daemon rebuild; a home under a symlink turned the no-op lane off; an unchecked exit status produced a number that had to be retracted (A-rows of 2026-11-11).

howto.task: Replace a blaze binary that may be running
howto.do: Remove the old file, then copy the new one; stop the old daemon by its pid first (a rebuilt blaze cannot stop an older daemon). Never `pkill -f`.
howto.why: macOS kills a process whose binary was overwritten in place (Killed: 9); `pkill -f` matches the calling shell.

howto.who: claude-fable-5-2 (Claude Fable 5.2), main agent in Claude Code
howto.task: Run lanes and test their work
howto.do: Lanes only write: one worktree and branch each, small commits, pushed often; no VM, no cargo, no daemon. The main agent runs `python3 -I harness/v2/integrate.py '{"branches":[...],"tests":true}'`: it merges every branch into the integration worktree, builds once, and prints one table (edit loop beside Relax, stale answers, new project, restart, memory, disk, tests). Failures go back to the lane whose files they name. The script's paths are the Mac's today (integration worktree /Volumes/Projects/blaze-int-1112, Relax at /tmp/relax-src); moving it to the one build VM is open.
howto.why: Rule fan-out-write-only as rewritten 2026-11-12: ten lanes each building in their own VM cost a cold build and hours each, and their numbers had to be redone on the combined tree anyway.

howto.task: Change or drive the harness ts kernel (crates/harness/mcp)
howto.do: In crates/harness/mcp: `bun install` (a new worktree has no node_modules), `bun test` (about 10 s; bunfig.toml preloads src/test-setup.ts, so no test reaches the live daemon or ~/.harness), `bunx tsc --noEmit`. Drive the real kernel from a shell with `bun scripts/cell.ts '{"cells": ["help()", "1 + 1"]}'` (a kernel of its own) or `{"sock": path, "cells": [...]}` for one started with HARNESS_REPL_SOCK=path. Decisions live in pure modules with their tests (patience.ts, stop.ts, notices.ts, disclose.ts, help.ts, journal.ts, shell-rule.ts); kernel.ts is the one API and mcp.ts/serve.ts only adapt it. A new function needs a `docs` entry beside it or functions/docs.test.ts fails. HARNESS_REPL_TYPECHECK=0 starts a kernel that does not type-check cells.
howto.why: Nothing here needs cargo or a VM, so this is the one place a lane runs its own tests; the end-to-end test (src/e2e.test.ts) starts the real MCP server, which is how a wrong reply is seen before an agent sees it.

howto.who: claude-fable-5-2 (Claude Fable 5.2), main agent in Claude Code
howto.task: Where work runs and where code is written
howto.do: One VM: `blaze-vm` (ix, arm64, 128 cores, 256 GiB committed, TTL 7 days from 2026-11-12; remake it with /tmp/blazevm.sh's steps: `ix new --name blaze-vm --no-shell --arch arm64 --cpus 128 --memory 256 --memory-commit --ttl 7d`, rustup + the pinned nightly, the pinned LLVM under /root/.blaze/native, `git clone` to /root/blaze, one release build, then /root/loop.sh and /root/lockwatch.sh). Build and run only through `ix shell blaze-vm --noninteractive -- /root/loop.sh <branch> <command...>`: one caller at a time, the branch checked out in /root/blaze, one incremental build, installed to /root/inst, the command run with BLAZE=/root/inst/blaze and BLAZE_HOME=/root/homes/<branch>, ten minutes at most; copy the binaries to /root/wt/<lane>/inst inside the call before measuring, keep projects and homes under /root/wt/<lane>/, start long runs as systemd units (export HOME=/root and PATH=/root/.cargo/bin:/run/current-system/sw/bin:$PATH in the unit's script) and poll them. One directory: lanes write in the integration checkout on the Mac (/Volumes/Projects/blaze-int-1112, branch int-1112), each in its own paths, without running git; the main agent commits, pushes and runs `harness/v2/integrate.py`. Timings name the load average and alternate base and new.
howto.why: Rules work-in-ix-vms, fan-out-write-only and worktree-per-lane as rewritten 2026-11-12: ten lane VMs and seventeen worktrees cost a cold build each and an hour of merging; a first shared queue on a 32-core VM (lanebase-1112) jammed for 22 minutes on a lock a daemon inherited, fixed in loop.sh (children start with the lock closed).

howto.task: Time blaze's edit loop on an ix VM
howto.do: Put BLAZE_HOME and the project on tmpfs (/dev/shm), and before the first measurement fill the VM's memory once so its hot-add is over (a script that holds about 116 GiB of bytes for a moment on a 128 GiB VM; MemTotal in /proc/meminfo stops growing). Alternate the binaries compared, at least two pairs, and compare pairs, not single runs; nothing else may run (no cargo, no second daemon). Memory numbers do not need any of this: they repeated within 2% from the first run. Check MemTotal again before each run: the host takes memory back from a VM that stops using it, and the rows are noisy while it does.
howto.why: On the VM's root disk a no-op run was 83 to 144 ms where tmpfs gives 17, and while virtio-mem was still adding memory (dmesg: `virtio_mem ... add_memory`, about 50 ms each, in bursts) the same binary's no-op build was 13.9 ms in one run and 81.4 in the next.

howto.task: Copy blaze's pinned LLVM from one ix VM to another
howto.do: ix shell <from> -- bash -c 'cd /root/.blaze/native && tar -cf - sha256-<hash> | zstd -9 -T8 -q' | ix shell <to> -- bash -c 'mkdir -p /root/.blaze/native && cd /root/.blaze/native && zstd -d -q | tar -xf -'
howto.why: Compressed in the pipe the 356 MB tree moved in under two minutes; uncompressed it took about 20 (rows records-6, edit2-3).

howto.do: Run `relax run --quiet <package>` from inside the package's directory, and check the exit status and the program's output of every run: from any other directory it prints `no Cargo.toml in ...`, exits 1 in 10 ms and still reports about 37 MB resident. `--verbose` prints each phase with its time; MAKEPAD_RUN_MEM_REPORT=1 the heap by subsystem (it raises the run's memory itself).
howto.why: The first Relax figure in this lane's brief (37.8 MB resident, 23.9 MB footprint, warm) was of such a failed run; a real warm run of hello-world is 87 MB resident, 50 MB footprint.

annoyances.where: APFS: writing into a clone just made
annoyances.what: On APFS the first `pwrite` into a file cloned a moment ago takes 3.5 ms whatever its size (4 KiB or 2.6 MB), and renaming that file over another takes 3.6 ms; a clone made 300 ms earlier takes 0.3 to 1 ms for the write and 0.3 ms for the rename, and a new sparse file 0.3 and 0.3 (python, 15 to 30 turns each, quiet disk). `F_FULLFSYNC` of any other file meanwhile makes them 10 and 7.5 ms. So an edit's place by clone, write, rename has a floor near 7 ms a file on a quiet disk.
